title: Slider design best practices
body:
Food for thought about sliders:

> Use a slider only when the precise value won’t matter to the user, but rather only the approximate range. Make sure that the users can select that range correctly without having to struggle too much to hit a precise value. In addition, any slider labels must be displayed above or beside the slider, rather than below it, in order to remain visible while the user is selecting a value. Alternatively, consider a different UI element that allows users to tap or even type to specify their choice rather than relying on press-and-drag gestures.

[Source](http://www.nngroup.com/articles/gui-slider-controls/)

In other words: we might have to rething the use-cases of where we advocate a slider in a UX perspective. I don't think our current slider implementation fits with the above guidelines.

What we could do:

* \[ ] Set a `snap` value by default, to not having to precisely select by the minimum unit (maybe automatically divide the whole range in X chunks)
* \[ ] Move both tooltips above the slider, so one can still see its value while sliding on a mobile
* \[ ] Allow one to specify an exact value (maybe directly in the tooltips. We talked about that already)
